title: VVS Laxman to Coach Indian Men's Team at 2026 Asian Games in Japan
excerpt: BCCI's Centre of Excellence head takes charge as Gambhir stays with the senior squad for the West Indies ODI series, replicating the split-coaching model that produced gold in Hangzhou.
body:
• VVS Laxman, BCCI's Centre of Excellence head, will coach the Indian men's cricket team at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan
  • Regular head coach Gautam Gambhir will remain with the senior squad for the home ODI series against the West Indies starting September 27
  • Shreyas Iyer will captain the men's side, with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi among the squad members; Harmanpreet Kaur leads the women's team
  • India's men's and women's teams both enter as defending T20 champions after winning gold at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games

VVS Laxman has been confirmed as head coach of the Indian men's cricket team for the 2026 Asian Games, the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced alongside the declaration of India's 768-member contingent for the Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

The appointment follows the same split-coaching model the BCCI used for the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, where Laxman guided the men's team to a gold medal. With the Asian Games cricket competition overlapping with India's home ODI series against the West Indies, head coach Gautam Gambhir will stay with the senior squad for the bilateral assignment beginning September 27.

Scheduling Conflict Forces Split

The cricket competition at the Asian Games begins September 24, with India's opening match scheduled four days later on September 28. Meanwhile, the first ODI against the West Indies is set for the same day, making it impossible for a single coaching setup to cover both assignments.

Laxman will be assisted by bowling coach Sunil Joshi, batting coach Hrishikesh Kanitkar, and Subhadeep Ghosh. The trio worked with Laxman during India's T20I series against Zimbabwe in July, when Gambhir was rested following the white-ball series in England.

"With multiple Indian teams likely to be in action simultaneously, it was important to distribute responsibilities. VVS Laxman's experience with India A and emerging players makes him the ideal choice for these assignments."

— BCCI Source

India Defend Double Gold

Both the Indian men's and women's teams enter the 2026 Asian Games as defending T20 champions. At the 2023 Hangzhou Games, Ruturaj Gaikwad led a largely second-string men's squad to gold, while Harmanpreet Kaur captained the women's team to the title.

This time, Shreyas Iyer will captain the men's side, with teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi among the squad members. Harmanpreet Kaur continues to lead the women's team, with Amol Muzumdar as head coach, assisted by bowling coach Aavishkar Salvi and fielding coach Munish Bali.

Tournament Draw and Venue

In the men's draw, India will face the second-placed side from Group A, which contains Afghanistan, Japan, and Nepal. The women's team enters the competition at the quarterfinal stage and will face Japan in their opener.

Cricket matches will be held at the newly constructed Korogi Sports Park, located roughly 40 minutes by train from central Nagoya. Japan Cricket Association CEO Naoki Alex Miyaji has noted limited hotel availability in the host area, with teams being provided hotel accommodations rather than the Athletes' Village.

Laxman's Track Record

Laxman has become the BCCI's go-to coaching option whenever parallel squads are required. As head of the Centre of Excellence, he has previously led Indian teams on bilateral tours and multi-sport events when the senior coaching staff has been unavailable. His familiarity with emerging players — many of whom have come through the India A programme — gives the younger squad members continuity in coaching relationships.

"VVS Laxman's experience with India A and emerging players makes him the ideal choice. He's a familiar face for many of the youngsters in the squad."

— BCCI Source

What's Next

The Asian Games 2026 run from September 19 to October 4. India will look to defend both T20 titles while Gambhir focuses on the West Indies series at home. The split-coaching arrangement underlines how compressed India's international calendar has become, with bilateral series, global events, and multi-sport competitions frequently overlapping.
